ai.issueType: Tab button references non-existent panel via aria-controls
ai.description: The aria-controls attribute references an ID "wrong-panel-${tab.id}" but the actual tabpanel element rendered at line 73 has id "panel-${tab.id}". This broken reference prevents assistive technologies from identifying which tabpanel is controlled by the tab button. This violates WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships).

ai.issueType: CustomButton uses div with role presentation instead of interactive element
ai.description: The CustomButton component renders a div with role="presentation" and an onClick handler. This removes the element from the accessibility tree while maintaining mouse-click behavior, making it unreachable to keyboard users and invisible to screen readers. It also lacks keyboard event handlers and tabindex. This violates WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: Decorative dot has non-descriptive aria-label
ai.description: The span element rendering a visual dot inside the Badge component has an aria-label containing only a bullet character ("●"). This does not convey meaningful information to screen reader users. If the dot indicates status (e.g., "active", "new"), it should have a descriptive label. If it is purely decorative, it should be hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden="true" to prevent confusing announcements.

ai.issueType: Date picker input missing required combobox attributes
ai.description: The date picker trigger input behaves as a combobox by opening a dialog popup but lacks the required role="combobox", dynamic aria-expanded state, and aria-controls reference. Screen readers cannot identify the element as a popup trigger, determine its expanded state, or associate it with the calendar dialog, violating SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: Dropdown toggle button missing aria-controls when collapsed
ai.description: The button conditionally sets aria-controls only when isOpen is true. The aria-controls attribute must reference the controlled listbox id consistently to maintain the programmatic relationship between the trigger and the popup, regardless of the expanded state.

ai.issueType: Navigation menu button has hardcoded aria-expanded and missing aria-controls
ai.description: The button uses aria-expanded={false} which is hardcoded and never updates when the menu opens/closes via setIsOpen, causing screen readers to always announce the menu as collapsed. Additionally, the button lacks aria-controls to programmatically associate it with the menu element it toggles (id={menuId}). This violates WCAG 4.1.2 (States, Properties) and 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships).

ai.issueType: Table data cell border fails non-text contrast requirements
ai.description: The table cell uses a bottom border with color #f3f4f6 (light gray). Against a typical white or light background, this provides insufficient contrast (approximately 1.03:1), failing WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast. Users with low vision may be unable to perceive the visual separation between table rows.

ai.issueType: Combobox input missing aria-describedby for error state
ai.description: The input uses aria-invalid to indicate error state but does not associate any error message text via aria-describedby. When error is true, screen reader users are informed the field is invalid but are not provided the specific error message content. If an error message element exists elsewhere in the component (not shown in snippet), it must be referenced. If no error text is displayed, this is a violation of SC 3.3.1 Error Identification.

ai.issueType: Progress bar animation lacks pause mechanism
ai.description: The progress bar includes an animated stripe pattern that runs continuously when animated=true and prefersReducedMotion is false. Per WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide, any moving content that lasts longer than 5 seconds must have a mechanism to pause, stop, or hide it. The animation runs indefinitely without user control.

ai.issueType: Skeleton component animation lacks reduced motion support
ai.description: The Skeleton component applies an infinite CSS animation automatically when mounted (when the animated prop is true, which is the default). This animation loops indefinitely, lasting longer than five seconds, and starts automatically without a mechanism for the user to pause, stop, or hide it. This violates WCAG SC 2.2.2. Additionally, the animation does not respect the prefers-reduced-motion media query, which can cause vestibular disorders for users sensitive to motion, violating SC 2.3.3.

ai.issueType: Modal close button lacks accessible name for screen reader users
ai.description: The close button inside the Modal component has visible text "Close" but screen reader users may not understand this button closes the dialog without additional context. WCAG 2.4.6 requires headings and labels to be descriptive. The button should indicate it closes the modal dialog specifically.

ai.issueType: Alert component dynamic message changes not announced via aria-live
ai.description: The Alert component uses role="alert" or role="status" but when the message prop changes dynamically, screen readers may not announce the update because aria-live is not explicitly set on the container. WCAG 4.1.3 requires status messages to be programmatically determinable. The role attribute alone is insufficient without aria-live.

ai.issueType: LoadingSpinner status changes not announced to assistive technologies
ai.description: The LoadingSpinner component has role="status" but lacks aria-live attribute, so when isLoading changes from false to true, screen reader users are not notified that loading has begun. WCAG 4.1.3 requires status messages to be available to assistive technologies. The spinner needs aria-live="polite" to announce loading state.

ai.issueType: Dropdown listbox options lack keyboard focus indicator styling
ai.description: The dropdown options use inline style for background color when focused but this only applies to the visually focused index, not keyboard focus state. WCAG 2.4.7 requires visible focus indicators for keyboard users. The tabIndex={-1} on options prevents them from receiving native focus, relying entirely on aria-activedescendant which needs visual correspondence.

ai.issueType: toggleRow function does not announce row selection changes to screen readers
ai.description: The toggleRow function changes row selection state but does not update any aria-live region. Screen reader users receive no feedback when selecting or deselecting individual rows, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages). This significantly degrades the experience for users who rely on assistive technology to track selection state changes.

ai.issueType: Empty table state message not announced when data becomes empty
ai.description: When sortedData.length === 0, the "No data" message is rendered but never announced to screen readers. This dynamic content change violates WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages). Users are not informed when the table transitions to an empty state, which could be misinterpreted as a loading or error condition.

ai.issueType: Checkbox input lacks visible label element
ai.description: The checkbox input at line 1023 has an aria-label attribute but no associated <label> element with a htmlFor attribute. This means sighted users cannot see what the checkbox is for, while screen reader users can. WCAG 3.3.2 requires labels or instructions for user input.

ai.issueType: Combobox listbox element not rendered in visible code
ai.description: The combobox input at line 1238 has aria-controls referencing listId (line 1205), but the listbox element with that id is not visible in this code snippet (code ends at line 1250). If the listbox is never rendered, aria-controls references a non-existent element, violating WCAG 4.1.2.

ai.issueType: Stepper button accessible name does not start with visible text
ai.description: The button's accessible name (aria-label) starts with "Step", but the visible text on the button itself is the step number (e.g., "1") or a checkmark. This violates SC 2.5.3 (Label in Name) because speech users expecting to say the visible label ("1") may fail if the name starts with "Step".

ai.issueType: Previous month button focus indicator removed
ai.description: The button has border: 'none' in its inline style without a visible alternative like outline or box-shadow. This removes the default focus indicator, making it difficult for keyboard users to identify focus, failing WCAG 2.4.7.

ai.issueType: Rating live region will not announce changes
ai.description: The live region uses aria-live="off" which completely disables announcements to screen readers. This defeats the purpose of having a live region for rating feedback. Users relying on screen readers will not hear when they focus on different star ratings or when the rating changes. This violates WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages).

ai.issueType: ColorPicker radiogroup container has unnecessary tabIndex
ai.description: The radiogroup div has tabIndex={0} making the container itself focusable. In a proper radiogroup pattern, only the individual radio buttons should be focusable, not the container. This creates an extra tab stop that serves no purpose and may confuse keyboard users. This relates to WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard).

ai.issueType: FileUpload button div missing aria-invalid for error state
ai.description: The visible button div (role="button") does not have aria-invalid when an error occurs. The aria-invalid is only on the hidden file input at line 1822, but screen reader users interacting with the visible button will not be informed of the validation error. The accessible interactive element must reflect the error state. This violates WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

ai.issueType: ColorPicker custom color text input aria-label does not match visible label
ai.description: The text input has aria-label="Hex color value" but the visible label text is "Custom:". Speech recognition users saying "click Custom" will not match the accessible name. Per WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name), the visible text should be included in the accessible name. This creates a barrier for voice control users.

ai.issueType: Skeleton animation ignores prefers-reduced-motion
ai.description: The skeleton component uses an infinite CSS animation (skeleton-shine 0.4s ease-in-out infinite) without checking for prefers-reduced-motion. Users with vestibular disorders or motion sensitivity may experience discomfort or disorientation from the continuous animation. This violates WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions) at Level AAA, but infinite animations that cannot be paused are increasingly treated as AA concerns under WCAG 2.2.

ai.issueType: Slider output element has aria-live="off" preventing value announcements
ai.description: The output element displaying the slider value has aria-live="off", which explicitly prevents screen readers from announcing value changes when the user adjusts the slider. Users who are blind or have low vision will not receive feedback about the current value as they interact with the control. This violates WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages) because dynamic value changes are not announced.

ai.issueType: CodeBlock copy button state changes not announced via aria-live region update
ai.description: The handleCopy function (lines 1987-1997) updates the copied and copyError state variables, which changes the button's aria-label and the live region text. However, the live region at lines 2003-2005 relies on React re-render to update, and there is no explicit focus management or aria-live assertion to ensure the status message is announced. Users may not receive confirmation that the copy action succeeded or failed. This violates WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages).

ai.issueType: Hex color text input pattern may reject valid user input without clear error messaging
ai.description: The text input has pattern="^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$" which enforces a specific format, but there is no visible error message or aria-invalid state when the pattern fails. Users who enter invalid hex values receive no feedback about why their input is rejected. This violates WCAG 3.3.1 (Error Identification) because errors are not clearly identified and described.

ai.issueType: Theme announcement timeout not cleared on re-render
ai.description: The setTimeout clearing the announcement message is not stored or cleared if the effect re-runs (e.g. rapid theme toggles). This can cause the new announcement to be cleared prematurely by the old timeout, failing SC 4.1.3.

ai.issueType: Auth restore success status not announced via live region
ai.description: The `useEffect` hook restores the user session from storage but only sets `isLoading` to false without updating `statusMsg`. The live region (Line 2351) transitions from "Authentication in progress" to an empty string, failing to announce the successful login state to screen reader users (WCAG 4.1.3).

ai.issueType: Auth restore error status suppressed by empty catch block
ai.description: The `catch` block inside `useEffect` is empty, silently swallowing JSON parse errors. Screen reader users are not informed if authentication restoration fails, leaving them unaware of their login status (WCAG 4.1.3).

ai.issueType: Sign in error state not handled or announced
ai.description: The `signIn` function lacks a `try/catch` block around the `await` operation. If the promise rejects, `setIsLoading(false)` is never called, leaving the live region stuck on "Authentication in progress" indefinitely (WCAG 4.1.3).
